Group A (30 students, avg 80%) & Group B (10 students, avg 60%). The combined weighted average is:
Why does taking a simple unweighted average of two group means give an incorrect result when group sizes differ?
questions.marking_scheme_answer: A simple average treats all groups as having equal weight. Larger groups contribute more total scores, so their average must carry proportionally higher weight.

Compare cluster-column charts and 100% stacked bar charts regarding their suitability for displaying expenditure data.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Cluster-column charts display absolute values side-by-side, making raw rupee comparisons easy. 100% stacked bar charts scale total height to 100%, isolating relative budget allocation percentages independent of total family income.

A motorist drives 100 km at 40 km/h and returns 100 km at 60 km/h. (a) Show why simple average speed (50 km/h) is wrong. (b) Calculate the correct average speed using weighted harmonic mean.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: (a) Simple average fails because more time is spent driving at 40 km/h than at 60 km/h. (b) Time outward = 100/40 = 2.5 h. Time return = 100/60 = 1.667 h. Total time = 4.167 h. Total distance = 200 km. Average Speed = 200 / 4.167 = 48.0 km/h (Harmonic mean formula: 2/(1/40 + 1/60) = 48 km/h).

questions.question_text: Case Study: Simpson's Paradox. Company X has two divisions. Division 1: Men pass rate 80% (100 applicants), Women 85% (20 applicants). Division 2: Men pass rate 30% (20 applicants), Women 35% (100 applicants). (a) Calculate overall pass rates for men and women. (b) Explain why women have higher rates in both divisions but lower overall rate.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: (a) Men passed = 0.80(100) + 0.30(20) = 80 + 6 = 86 out of 120 (71.7%). Women passed = 0.85(20) + 0.35(100) = 17 + 35 = 52 out of 120 (43.3%). (b) Simpson's paradox: Most women applied to Division 2 which had a much lower passing rate overall, heavily weighting their aggregate average downwards.

Milk solution A (4 liters, 20% water) is mixed with solution B (6 liters, 30% water) and solution C (5 liters, pure water). Find the final percentage of water in the 15-liter mixture.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Water in A = 0.20 * 4 = 0.8 L. Water in B = 0.30 * 6 = 1.8 L. Water in C = 1.00 * 5 = 5.0 L. Total water = 0.8 + 1.8 + 5.0 = 7.6 L. Total volume = 15 L. Water % = (7.6 / 15) * 100 = 50.67%.

questions.question_text: Case Study: Daily Activity Budgeting. A worker logs daily hours: Sleep 8h, Work 8h, Recreation 4h, Chores 4h. (a) Is a 24-hour daily activity stacked bar chart visually identical to a 100% stacked bar chart? Explain. (b) Convert the hours to percentages.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: (a) Yes, because the total sum for every individual is constant at 24 hours (100% of a day). Scaling to 100% preserves exact bar proportions. (b) Sleep = 8/24 = 33.33%, Work = 8/24 = 33.33%, Recreation = 4/24 = 16.67%, Chores = 4/24 = 16.67%. Sum = 100%.

questions.question_text: In a 100% stacked bar chart, if a component slice doubles in rupee value while all other components also double, its slice percentage:
Explain why proportional scaling preserves slice percentages in a 100% stacked bar chart.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: If all component values are multiplied by factor k, both component value and total sum increase by k. The ratio (k * component) / (k * total) cancels k, keeping percentage unchanged.

questions.question_text: A student scores 70 in Test 1 (weight 1), 80 in Test 2 (weight 2), and x in Test 3 (weight 3). If weighted mean is 85, find x.
A car travels 30 km at 30 km/h, 40 km at 40 km/h, and 50 km at 50 km/h. Calculate total time taken and average speed across the 120 km journey.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Time t1 = 30/30 = 1 h. t2 = 40/40 = 1 h. t3 = 50/50 = 1 h. Total time = 3 hours. Total distance = 120 km. Average Speed = 120 / 3 = 40 km/h.

questions.question_text: Case Study: Environmental Pollution Aggregation. Region 1 (area 100 sq km) has air pollutant concentration 40 ppm. Region 2 (area 300 sq km) has 80 ppm. Region 3 (area 100 sq km) has 100 ppm. (a) Calculate area-weighted mean pollution concentration. (b) Explain why simple average (73.33 ppm) misleads environmental policymakers.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: (a) Weighted Mean = (100*40 + 300*80 + 100*100) / (100 + 300 + 100) = (4000 + 24000 + 10000) / 500 = 38000 / 500 = 76.0 ppm. (b) Simple average underestimates total exposure because the largest land area (Region 2, 300 sq km) has high pollution (80 ppm) and carries 60% of total geographic weight.
